RULES:
- Read EXHAUSTIVELY but efficiently: use grep/Glob to locate, then Read the relevant spans. NEVER read these (huge/generated, will waste context): _dectc_codegen/*.cudafe1.cpp (581K lines each), .build_cache/, __pycache__/, *.so, third_party/cutlass.
- Cite EVERY non-obvious claim as file:line. Prefer ACTUAL CONFIGURED VALUES over prose (real numbers: model dims, layer counts, vocab, seq len, step budgets, seeds, tile sizes, register counts).
- Write a thorough markdown digest to /workspace/phase0/<NAME>.md (full detail, this is the persisted artifact). Then return the structured summary (the digest_path field = that path).
- The "prompt_contradictions" field is load-bearing: list anywhere the SuperGrok2 prompt's stated assumptions disagree with the live code. For existing components the CODEBASE WINS; your job is to SURFACE the disagreement, not resolve it.

SUBSYSTEM: The Hopper tensor-core substrate (WGMMA/TMA) + model GEMM stages.
Files: csrc/backends/cuda/sm_90/{mma.cuh, wgmma.cuh, primitives.cuh, tile_pipeline.cuh, warp_specialize.cuh, wgmma_selftest.cu}; csrc/fused/sm_90/{model_stage_decoder_tc.cuh, model_stage_vit_tc.cuh, model_stage_mamba3.cuh, *_layout.cuh}; CUTLASS usage.
EXTRACT (file:line): how WGMMA + TMA (cp.async.bulk) are emitted (inline PTX vs CUTLASS Sm90 collectives); the TF32 path for FP32; warp-specialized producer/consumer (setmaxnreg); the claim that WGMMA shows up as HGMMA in SASS and TMA as UTMALDG; whether FP8/FP4/NVFP4 paths exist in the kernels. Note the known dead CUTLASS TF32 A-transposed RS GEMM (runtime-dead scalar fallback) from .audit_notes.md if you can find it.

Key SuperGrok2-prompt assertions to check against the code (flag any that are wrong):
- "33 megakernels / 33 cells" exist (11 optimizers x 3 models on sm_90).
- "44 -> 99 component architecture".
- "single-source math contract + drift guard" enforced.
- "fused-megakernel substrate": one persistent kernel, fwd->barrier->bwd->barrier->opt, single launch.
- The mod-97 tasks are the CURRENT data; Phase 3 will replace them with FineWeb-Edu (decoder), ImageNet-1k (ViT), GiftEvalPretrain (Mamba).
- evaluate() currently forwards the WHOLE held-out tensor every call (fine at mod-97 ~4656 samples, catastrophic at scale).
- EarlyStopper currently triggers on 95% test accuracy (no analog for LM/forecasting).
- "MultiGPUTimingPool" exists (compile.py:4874) and is the cross-GPU timing pool.
- Parallelism strategy is "already in the codebase" (do not redesign).

146	//  Swizzle mode (PTX ISA §<ip>.4, descriptor bits 62-61 "swizzle mode").
147	//
148	//  The shared-memory matrix descriptor encodes how the 128-bit core-matrix
149	//  rows are interleaved in smem to avoid bank conflicts on the wgmma read.
150	//  CRITICAL: the descriptor's layout_type field (bits 63:62) does NOT use a
151	//  size-ascending encoding. The hardware/CUTLASS encoding is
152	//  (cute/arch/mma_sm90_desc.hpp LayoutType, verified):
153	//    NONE/INTERLEAVE = 0,  SWIZZLE_128B = 1,  SWIZZLE_64B = 2,  SWIZZLE_32B = 3.
154	//  (An earlier draft had 32B=1/128B=3 swapped; the correctness path uses NONE=0
155	//  so it was unaffected, but the perf-phase swizzle modes MUST use these values.)
156	//
157	//  CORRECTNESS-PATH NOTE (deviation flagged in the report): the gated /
158	//  tested numerics path ships swizzle = NONE (kSwizzleNone). NONE is a
159	//  fully-legal descriptor mode (§<ip>.4) and is the layout the
160	//  correctness gates validate against torch. The 128B-swizzle layout is a
161	//  PERF-PHASE optimization (bank-conflict elimination on the smem read) and
162	//  is exposed here as the template parameter the model headers will select
163	//  once the quiet-GPU perf phase measures it; it is NOT required for any
164	//  correctness gate. See DESIGN §4.1 ("specify the 128-byte-swizzle layout"
165	//  is the perf target; phase-1 staging uses cp.async, §4.1 item 3).
166	// =========================================================================
167	enum SwizzleMode : uint32_t {
168	    kSwizzleNone = 0,   // INTERLEAVE / no swizzle (the correctness-path layout)
169	    kSwizzle128B = 1,   // SWIZZLE_128B
170	    kSwizzle64B  = 2,   // SWIZZLE_64B
171	    kSwizzle32B  = 3,   // SWIZZLE_32B

174	// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
175	//  generic-smem-pointer → matrix-descriptor start address.
176	//  PTX ISA §<ip>.4: the descriptor's bits 13-0 hold the start address of
177	//  the matrix in shared memory, encoded as the 18-bit smem byte address with
178	//  the low 4 bits dropped — i.e. addr_field = (smem_byte_addr & 0x3FFFF) >> 4.
179	//  The low 4 bits MUST be zero (16-byte alignment) or they are silently lost.
180	// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
181	__device__ __forceinline__ uint32_t smem_desc_encode_addr(const void* smem_ptr) {
182	#if defined(__CUDA_ARCH__) && (__CUDA_ARCH__ >= 900)
183	    uint32_t a = static_cast<uint32_t>(__cvta_generic_to_shared(smem_ptr));
184	    return (a & 0x3FFFFu) >> 4;
185	#else
186	    (void)smem_ptr;
187	    return 0u;
188	#endif
189	}

191	// =========================================================================
192	//  Shared-memory matrix descriptor (PTX ISA §<ip>.4).
193	//
194	//  64-bit layout (bit ranges per the ISA table):
195	//    bits  13: 0  start address (smem byte addr >> 4)
196	//    bits  15:14  (reserved / 0)
197	//    bits  29:16  leading-dimension byte offset (LBO) >> 4
198	//    bits  31:30  (reserved / 0)
199	//    bits  45:32  stride-dimension byte offset (SBO) >> 4
200	//    bits  48:46  (reserved / 0)
201	//    bits  51:49  matrix base offset (for swizzle; 0 for our tiles)
202	//    bits  61:52  (reserved / 0)
203	//    bits  63:62  swizzle / layout mode (0 none / 1 128B / 2 64B / 3 32B —
204	//                 the CUTLASS LayoutType encoding, see SwizzleMode above)
205	//
206	//  LBO and SBO are the byte offsets between consecutive "core matrices" along
207	//  the leading and stride dimensions respectively (§<ip>.3 "Strides").
208	//  Both are encoded >>4 (16-byte granular). The exact (LBO,SBO) depend on the
209	//  operand's smem tile layout; the make_desc_*_kmajor builders below compute
210	//  them for the canonical row-major-K bf16 tiles the model headers stage.
211	// =========================================================================
212	struct SmemDesc {
213	    uint64_t desc;
214	};
215	
216	// Low-level builder: caller supplies LBO/SBO in BYTES; we apply the >>4 and
217	// the swizzle field. Use the make_desc_*_kmajor convenience wrappers unless
218	// you have a bespoke smem layout.
219	template <SwizzleMode Swizzle = kSwizzleNone>
220	__device__ __forceinline__ SmemDesc make_smem_desc(
221	    const void* smem_base, uint32_t lbo_bytes, uint32_t sbo_bytes,
222	    uint32_t base_offset = 0u
223	) {
224	    SmemDesc d;
225	#if defined(__CUDA_ARCH__) && (__CUDA_ARCH__ >= 900)
226	    uint64_t addr = static_cast<uint64_t>(smem_desc_encode_addr(smem_base));
227	    uint64_t lbo  = static_cast<uint64_t>((lbo_bytes >> 4) & 0x3FFFu);
228	    uint64_t sbo  = static_cast<uint64_t>((sbo_bytes >> 4) & 0x3FFFu);
229	    uint64_t bo   = static_cast<uint64_t>(base_offset & 0x7u);
230	    uint64_t sw   = static_cast<uint64_t>(Swizzle & 0x3u);
231	    d.desc = (addr)                 // bits 13:0
232	           | (lbo << 16)            // bits 29:16
233	           | (sbo << 32)            // bits 45:32
234	           | (bo  << 49)            // bits 51:49
235	           | (sw  << 62);           // bits 63:62
236	#else
237	    (void)smem_base; (void)lbo_bytes; (void)sbo_bytes; (void)base_offset;
238	    d.desc = 0;
239	#endif
240	    return d;
241	}

256	//  row-major block of 128-bit rows: core-matrix 0 (k 0..7) occupies the first
257	//  MN*8 bf16 (MN*16 bytes), core-matrix 1 (k 8..15) the next MN*16 bytes.

291	//  fp32 accumulator fragment for an m64×N output tile.
292	//  PTX ISA §<ip>.3 "Register fragment for .f32 accumulators" (the
293	//  m64nNk16 wgmma writes its output across the 128 warpgroup threads).
294	//
295	//  Fragment layout (the ISA figure, decoded):
296	//    - 128 threads = 4 warps; the M=64 rows are split so that
297	//        warp w  (w in 0..3)  owns rows  [16*w .. 16*w+15],
298	//      and within a warp, lane L owns two row-groups:
299	//        row_hi = 16*w + (L/4)        (rows 0..7 of the warp's block)
300	//        row_lo = row_hi + 8          (rows 8..15)
301	//    - The N columns are held as N/2 fp32 registers per thread, in pairs:
302	//        register pair (2c, 2c+1) holds columns (col_base+0, col_base+1)
303	//        where col_base = (L%4)*2 + 8*(c/2_grouped)...  [the (col%8) + 8*(c>>1)
304	//      grouping of the ISA]. We expose the exact decode via frag_row()/
305	//      frag_col() so the epilogue (and the self-test) maps register i of
306	//      lane L (in warp w) to the (row,col) of the 64×N output it represents.
307	//
308	//  We store N/2 floats. c[2*g + p] is the p-th (p in {0,1}) of register-group
309	//  g (g in [0, N/4) for the "even/odd column pair" grouping). The helpers
310	//  frag_row(lane,i) / frag_col(lane,i) give the global (row,col) so a single
311	//  authoritative decode is shared by the epilogue store AND the gate's
312	//  reference comparison (no chance of a mismatched private decode).
313	// =========================================================================
314	template <int N>
315	struct WgmmaAccum {
316	    static_assert(N % 8 == 0, "wgmma N must be a multiple of 8");
317	    static constexpr int kRegs = N / 2;   // fp32 regs per thread
318	    float c[kRegs];
319	
320	    __device__ __forceinline__ void zero() {
321	        #pragma unroll
322	        for (int i = 0; i < kRegs; ++i) c[i] = 0.0f;
323	    }
324	};

326	// --- Authoritative fragment decode (PTX ISA §<ip>.3, .f32 accumulators) -
327	// For thread `tid_in_wg` in [0,128) and register index `i` in [0, N/2):
328	//   warp = tid_in_wg / 32 ; lane = tid_in_wg % 32.
329	//   The 64 M-rows are partitioned warp-major: rows [16*warp, 16*warp+16).
330	//   lane bits decode within the warp's 16-row × N block as in the ISA figure:
331	//     group g = i / 2 ; sub p = i % 2.
332	//     row = 16*warp + (lane / 4) + 8 * (g % 2 == 0 ? 0 : 0)   -- see below.
333	//
334	// The ISA C-fragment for .m64nNk16.f32 lays out each lane's N/2 elements as
335	// (over the row pair r0=lane/4, r1=r0+8) interleaved column pairs. The precise
336	// closed form, validated by the A=I gate, is:
337	//   group_of_8 = i / 8 ;   within = i % 8
338	//   row = 16*warp + (lane/4) + 8*(within / 4)
339	//   col = (lane%4)*2 + (within % 2) + 8*group_of_8 + ...
340	// To keep ONE source of truth that the gate verifies bit-for-bit, the decode
341	// is implemented below in the exact factored form the ISA figure gives for
342	// the 16x8 sub-blocks the f32 accumulator tiles across N.
343	__device__ __forceinline__ void wgmma_frag_decode(
344	    int tid_in_wg, int i, int N, int& row, int& col
345	) {
346	    const int warp = tid_in_wg >> 5;       // 0..3
347	    const int lane = tid_in_wg & 31;       // 0..31
348	    // Each 16x8 output sub-block (one "n8" column slab) contributes 4 regs
349	    // per thread (8 rows split into 2 row-halves × ... ). The ISA's .f32
350	    // fragment for an n8 slab gives, per lane:
351	    //   reg 0 -> (row = lane/4,       col = (lane%4)*2 + 0)
352	    //   reg 1 -> (row = lane/4,       col = (lane%4)*2 + 1)
353	    //   reg 2 -> (row = lane/4 + 8,   col = (lane%4)*2 + 0)
354	    //   reg 3 -> (row = lane/4 + 8,   col = (lane%4)*2 + 1)
355	    // and successive n8 slabs add 8 to the column. With N columns there are
356	    // N/8 slabs × 4 regs = N/2 regs (matches kRegs).
357	    const int slab   = i >> 2;             // which n8 column slab (0..N/8-1)
358	    const int within = i & 3;              // 0..3 within the slab
359	    const int row_half = within >> 1;      // 0 -> rows 0..7, 1 -> rows 8..15
360	    const int col_par  = within & 1;       // 0 or 1 column within the pair
361	    row = 16 * warp + (lane >> 2) + 8 * row_half;
362	    col = (lane & 3) * 2 + col_par + 8 * slab;
363	    (void)N;
364	}

596	//

600	//  issue uses ScaleD=0 (overwrite, so the accumulator need not be pre-zeroed
601	//  for a fresh tile); subsequent issues accumulate (ScaleD=1). One
602	//  wgmma_fence() before the group, one commit_group()+wait_group<0>() after.

605	//  advances the smem base / pipeline stage between k-steps). Keeping the
606	//  descriptor generation a callback is what lets the SAME mainloop serve the
607	//  unpipelined gate (gen reads a fixed pre-staged tile array) and the

618	          typename DescGen>

620	    WgmmaAccum<N>& acc, int k_steps, DescGen gen
621	) {
622	#if defined(__CUDA_ARCH__) && (__CUDA_ARCH__ >= 900)
623	    if (FenceBeforeFirst) wgmma_fence();
624	    // First k-step OVERWRITES (ScaleD=0) so a fresh accumulator is correct
625	    // without a separate zero. (If the caller wants to accumulate onto a
626	    // pre-existing fp32 value, it sets FenceBeforeFirst=false, zeroes/sets the
627	    // accumulator + fences itself, and we still issue k=0 below — but then the
628	    // caller should pass an accumulating first step; for the common fresh-tile
629	    // path this is exactly D = sum_k A_k B_k.)
630	    {
631	        auto d = gen(0);
632	        wgmma_m64nNk16_bf16<N, /*ScaleD=*/0, TransA, TransB>(acc, d.first, d.second);
633	    }
634	    #pragma unroll 1
635	    for (int k = 1; k < k_steps; ++k) {
636	        auto d = gen(k);
637	        wgmma_m64nNk16_bf16<N, /*ScaleD=*/1, TransA, TransB>(acc, d.first, d.second);
638	    }
639	    wgmma_commit_group();
640	    wgmma_wait_group<0>();
641	#else
642	    (void)acc; (void)k_steps; (void)gen;
643	#endif
644	}

100	//  Ring-buffer geometry for one (A 64×16 + B N×16) bf16 stage.
101	//  A tile: 64×16 bf16 = 2048 B.  B tile: N×16 bf16 = N*32 B.
102	//  All tiles K-contiguous (row-major), matching make_desc_{A,B}_kmajor.
103	// =========================================================================
104	template <int N>
105	struct TileGeom {
106	    static constexpr int kAElems   = 64 * kWgmmaAtomK;        // 1024
107	    static constexpr int kBElems   = N  * kWgmmaAtomK;        // N*16
108	    static constexpr int kABytes   = kAElems * (int)sizeof(__nv_bfloat16);
109	    static constexpr int kBBytes   = kBElems * (int)sizeof(__nv_bfloat16);
110	    static constexpr int kStageBytes = kABytes + kBBytes;
111	    static constexpr uint32_t kARowStride = kWgmmaAtomK * (uint32_t)sizeof(__nv_bfloat16); // 32
112	    static constexpr uint32_t kBRowStride = kWgmmaAtomK * (uint32_t)sizeof(__nv_bfloat16); // 32
113	    // tx-bytes for the stage's two cp.async transactions (full barrier expects).
114	    static constexpr int kStageTxBytes = kStageBytes;
115	};

117	// =========================================================================
118	//  TilePipeline — the Depth-stage ring + its mbarriers.
119	//
120	//  smem layout the caller hands us (one contiguous arena, 16B-aligned):
121	//    [ stage0 A | stage0 B | stage1 A | stage1 B | ... | full[Depth] | empty[Depth] ]
122	//  where each stage's A is 16B-aligned (kAElems is a multiple of 8 bf16 = 16B)
123	//  and B follows (also 16B-multiple for the design's N). The two mbarrier
124	//  arrays are 8-byte words.
125	//
126	//  Two barriers per stage (the canonical producer/consumer ring):
127	//    full[s]  : producer arrives (expect_tx) when it has issued the loads for
128	//               stage s; consumer waits on it before issuing wgmma.
129	//    empty[s] : consumer arrives when it has finished consuming stage s;
130	//               producer waits on it before overwriting stage s (so the
131	//               in-flight wgmma is not clobbered). For Depth-buffering the
132	//               producer can run Depth stages ahead before it must wait.
133	//
134	//  Phase parity: each barrier flips parity every time its expected arrivals
135	//  complete. We track per-stage parity bits for full and empty.
136	// =========================================================================
137	//  NOTE on storage: Mbarrier (warp_specialize.cuh) is a thin wrapper around a
138	//  single smem word and has only an `explicit Mbarrier(ull*)` constructor (no
139	//  default ctor). To avoid needing a default-constructible barrier array, we
140	//  store ONLY the barrier-word base pointer and construct an Mbarrier
141	//  on-demand via full(s) / empty(s) — a zero-cost wrapper around the word.
142	template <int N, int Depth>
143	struct TilePipeline {
144	    __nv_bfloat16* ring;          // [Depth] × (A|B) tiles, 16B-aligned
145	    unsigned long long* bars;     // [2*Depth] mbarrier words: full[Depth] then empty[Depth]
146	
147	    // Construct over a caller-provided smem arena. `arena` points at the start
148	    // of the ring (must be 16B-aligned). The barrier words follow the tiles.
149	    __device__ __forceinline__ TilePipeline(void* arena)
150	        : ring(reinterpret_cast<__nv_bfloat16*>(arena)),
151	          bars(reinterpret_cast<unsigned long long*>(
152	              reinterpret_cast<char*>(arena) +
153	              (size_t)Depth * TileGeom<N>::kStageBytes)) {}
154	
155	    __device__ __forceinline__ Mbarrier full(int s)  { return Mbarrier(bars + s); }
156	    __device__ __forceinline__ Mbarrier empty(int s) { return Mbarrier(bars + Depth + s); }
157	
158	    __device__ __forceinline__ __nv_bfloat16* stageA(int s) {
159	        return ring + (size_t)s * (TileGeom<N>::kAElems + TileGeom<N>::kBElems);
160	    }
161	    __device__ __forceinline__ __nv_bfloat16* stageB(int s) {
162	        return stageA(s) + TileGeom<N>::kAElems;
163	    }
164	
165	    // Bytes the caller must allocate as dynamic smem for this pipeline.
166	    static constexpr size_t smem_bytes() {
167	        return (size_t)Depth * TileGeom<N>::kStageBytes +
168	               (size_t)2 * Depth * sizeof(unsigned long long);
169	    }
170	
171	    // Init the barriers (one thread of the block). Each barrier expects a FULL
172	    // WARPGROUP (128) of arrivals per phase: full[] is arrived by all 128
173	    // producer threads (so the phase-flip happens-after every thread's
174	    // cp.async + wait_group, giving the consumer a warpgroup-wide visibility
175	    // guarantee), empty[] by all 128 consumer threads. (An earlier draft used
176	    // init(1) + a per-warp elect_one_sync arrive — but elect.sync elects one
177	    // leader PER WARP, so 4 warps produced 4 arrivals on a count-1 barrier,
178	    // flipping the phase an even number of times and DEADLOCKING the consumer's
179	    // try_wait.parity. count=128 + all-threads-arrive is the correct contract.)
180	    __device__ __forceinline__ void init_barriers() {
181	        if (threadIdx.x == 0) {
182	            #pragma unroll
183	            for (int s = 0; s < Depth; ++s) {
184	                full(s).init(128);
185	                empty(s).init(128);
186	            }
187	        }
188	    }
189	};

191	// =========================================================================
192	//  Producer-side staging of ONE K-tile (stage `slot`, k-index `k`) via
193	//  cp.async (DESIGN §4.2 WG0). Issues 16-byte cp.async copies of the A and B
194	//  tiles from HBM into the ring slot, then the elected leader does
195	//  arrive_expect_tx(tx) on the stage's `full` barrier so the consumer knows
196	//  the bytes are inbound. cp.async + mbarrier transaction-count is the
197	//  standard Hopper async-load handshake.
198	//
199	//  NOTE: this uses cp.async (.cg.16), NOT TMA — DESIGN §4.1 item 3 makes TMA
200	//  explicitly phase-2; phase-1 staging is cp.async (already overlaps load
201	//  latency). For cp.async the transaction completion is signalled via
202	//  cp.async.mbarrier.arrive (the bytes are counted by the barrier). We model
203	//  that with arrive_expect_tx on the producer leader + cp_async_commit, and
204	//  the consumer's try_wait/parity gates on it.
205	// =========================================================================
206	template <int N, int Depth>
207	__device__ __forceinline__ void pipeline_produce_ktile(
208	    TilePipeline<N, Depth>& pipe, int slot, int k,
209	    const __nv_bfloat16* gA, const __nv_bfloat16* gB, int /*k_steps*/
210	) {
211	#if defined(__CUDA_ARCH__) && (__CUDA_ARCH__ >= 900)
212	    const int wtid = threadIdx.x & 127;          // 0..127 within WG0
213	    __nv_bfloat16* dA = pipe.stageA(slot);
214	    __nv_bfloat16* dB = pipe.stageB(slot);
215	    const __nv_bfloat16* sA = gA + (size_t)k * TileGeom<N>::kAElems;  // row-major MxK
216	    const __nv_bfloat16* sB = gB + (size_t)k * TileGeom<N>::kBElems;  // row-major NxK
217	
218	    // 16B (8 bf16) cp.async copies SCATTERED into the canonical Major-K layout
219	    // (two stacked 8-wide core matrices) make_desc_*_kmajor requires. A global
220	    // row (mn, 0..15) splits into two 16B halves: half 0 (k 0..7) lands at
221	    // mn*8, half 1 (k 8..15) at MN*8 + mn*8 — both 16B-aligned. kVec=8 bf16.
222	    constexpr int kVec = 16 / (int)sizeof(__nv_bfloat16);   // 8 bf16 / 16B
223	    // A: MN=64. 64 rows × 2 halves = 128 vectors.
224	    constexpr int kAHalves = 64 * (kWgmmaAtomK / kVec);     // 64*2 = 128
225	    for (int v = wtid; v < kAHalves; v += 128) {
226	        const int mn = v >> 1;                  // 0..63
227	        const int half = v & 1;                 // 0 or 1
228	        const __nv_bfloat16* src = sA + (size_t)mn * kWgmmaAtomK + (size_t)half * kVec;
229	        __nv_bfloat16* dst = dA + (size_t)half * (64 * kVec) + (size_t)mn * kVec;
230	        prim::cp_async_cg_16(dst, src);
231	    }
232	    // B: MN=N. N rows × 2 halves vectors.
233	    constexpr int kBHalves = N * (kWgmmaAtomK / kVec);      // N*2
234	    for (int v = wtid; v < kBHalves; v += 128) {
235	        const int mn = v >> 1;                  // 0..N-1
236	        const int half = v & 1;
237	        const __nv_bfloat16* src = sB + (size_t)mn * kWgmmaAtomK + (size_t)half * kVec;
238	        __nv_bfloat16* dst = dB + (size_t)half * (N * kVec) + (size_t)mn * kVec;
239	        prim::cp_async_cg_16(dst, src);
240	    }
241	    prim::cp_async_commit();
242	    // Drain THIS stage's group before signalling full, so the consumer's wgmma
243	    // (which reads smem directly, not through the mbarrier transaction count)
244	    // sees landed bytes. cp.async.wait_group<0> + the arrive gives a correct
245	    // handshake without relying on cp.async.mbarrier.arrive byte-counting
246	    // (which would require the .mbarrier.arrive variant; we keep the portable
247	    // wait_group form from primitives.cuh and use the mbarrier purely as the
248	    // cross-warpgroup ready signal). DESIGN §4.2: one async-proxy fence per
249	    // hand-off.
250	    prim::cp_async_wait_group<0>();
251	    fence_async_proxy();
252	    // ALL 128 producer threads arrive (barrier count=128). Each thread's
253	    // arrive happens-after its own cp.async + wait_group<0>, so the phase-flip
254	    // (on the 128th arrive) is visibility-ordered after every staged byte.
255	    pipe.full(slot).arrive();       // signal: stage `slot` is ready to consume
256	#else
257	    (void)pipe; (void)slot; (void)k; (void)gA; (void)gB;
258	#endif
259	}

261	// =========================================================================
262	//  tc_pipelined_gemm_m64nNk16 — the turnkey single-CTA pipelined GEMM.
263	//  blockDim.x = 256: WG0 = producer (tid 0..127), WG1 = consumer (128..255).
264	//  DESIGN §4.2 producer/consumer structure, §4.3 occupancy budget.
265	//
266	//  Determinism: the consumer issues wgmma in ASCENDING k (fixed order); the
267	//  pipeline only changes operand-availability timing, not the reduction order,
268	//  so the fp32 accumulation is bit-identical to the unpipelined kchain
269	//  (DESIGN gate c).
270	// =========================================================================
271	template <int N, int Depth>
272	__device__ __forceinline__ void tc_pipelined_gemm_m64nNk16(
273	    const __nv_bfloat16* __restrict__ gA,
274	    const __nv_bfloat16* __restrict__ gB,
275	    float* __restrict__ gD, int k_steps
276	) {
277	#if defined(__CUDA_ARCH__) && (__CUDA_ARCH__ >= 900)
278	    extern __shared__ char smem_raw[];
279	    // 16B-align the ring arena.
280	    uintptr_t base = reinterpret_cast<uintptr_t>(smem_raw);
281	    uintptr_t aligned = (base + 15u) & ~uintptr_t(15u);
282	    TilePipeline<N, Depth> pipe(reinterpret_cast<void*>(aligned));
283	    pipe.init_barriers();
284	    __syncthreads();
285	
286	    const int warpgroup = threadIdx.x / 128;    // 0 = producer, 1 = consumer
287	    const bool is_producer = (warpgroup == 0);
288	
289	    // Register rebalance (DESIGN §4.2): producer few regs, consumer many.
290	    // Guarded by SG_TUNED_*_REGS != 0 (0 disables for portability/debug).
291	#if (SG_TUNED_PROD_REGS != 0) && (SG_TUNED_CONS_REGS != 0)
292	    if (is_producer) warpgroup_reg_dealloc<SG_TUNED_PROD_REGS>();
293	    else             warpgroup_reg_alloc  <SG_TUNED_CONS_REGS>();
294	#endif
295	
296	    if (is_producer) {
297	        // Producer: stage every K-tile in ascending k. With Depth buffering it
298	        // may run up to Depth stages ahead; we gate reuse of a slot on the
299	        // consumer having released it (empty[slot]).
300	        unsigned empty_parity[Depth];
301	        #pragma unroll
302	        for (int s = 0; s < Depth; ++s) empty_parity[s] = 0u;
303	        for (int k = 0; k < k_steps; ++k) {
304	            const int slot = k % Depth;
305	            // For k >= Depth, the slot was used by k-Depth; wait until the
306	            // consumer released it (empty barrier) before overwriting.
307	            if (k >= Depth) {
308	                pipe.empty(slot).wait(empty_parity[slot]);
309	                empty_parity[slot] ^= 1u;
310	            }
311	            pipeline_produce_ktile<N, Depth>(pipe, slot, k, gA, gB, k_steps);
312	        }
313	    } else {
314	        // Consumer: wgmma over each staged K-tile in ascending k. The fp32
315	        // fragment accumulates across the whole chain (first k overwrites).
316	        WgmmaAccum<N> acc;
317	        unsigned full_parity[Depth];
318	        #pragma unroll
319	        for (int s = 0; s < Depth; ++s) full_parity[s] = 0u;
320	
321	        // We can't use the kchain helper directly (it expects all descriptors
322	        // available); instead we inline the SAME choreography: one fence, then
323	        // k=0 overwrite / k>0 accumulate, commit+wait at the end. Issuing each
324	        // wgmma right after its stage is ready overlaps load and compute.
325	        wgmma_fence();
326	        for (int k = 0; k < k_steps; ++k) {
327	            const int slot = k % Depth;
328	            pipe.full(slot).wait(full_parity[slot]);
329	            full_parity[slot] ^= 1u;
330	
331	            __nv_bfloat16* aTile = pipe.stageA(slot);
332	            __nv_bfloat16* bTile = pipe.stageB(slot);
333	            SmemDesc dA = make_desc_A_kmajor</*M=*/64, kSwizzleNone>(aTile);
334	            SmemDesc dB = make_desc_B_kmajor</*N=*/N,  kSwizzleNone>(bTile);
335	            // Both operands Major-K ⇒ TransA=0, TransB=0 (cute Major::K == 0).
336	            if (k == 0) {
337	                wgmma_m64nNk16_bf16<N, /*ScaleD=*/0, /*TransA=*/0, /*TransB=*/0>(acc, dA, dB);
338	            } else {
339	                wgmma_m64nNk16_bf16<N, /*ScaleD=*/1, /*TransA=*/0, /*TransB=*/0>(acc, dA, dB);
340	            }
341	            // Commit + wait THIS issue before releasing the slot, so the
342	            // producer does not overwrite operands the async wgmma still reads.
343	            wgmma_commit_group();
344	            wgmma_wait_group<0>();
345	            // Release the slot back to the producer. ALL 128 consumer threads
346	            // arrive (barrier count=128) — see init_barriers: the per-warp elect
347	            // would give 4 arrivals on a count-1 barrier and deadlock.
348	            pipe.empty(slot).arrive();
349	        }
350	
351	        // Epilogue: store the fp32 fragment. The consumer warpgroup owns the
352	        // output; decode relative to its 128-thread group (tid-128).
353	        const int tid_in_wg = threadIdx.x - 128;
354	        #pragma unroll
355	        for (int i = 0; i < WgmmaAccum<N>::kRegs; ++i) {
356	            int row, col;
357	            wgmma_frag_decode(tid_in_wg, i, N, row, col);
358	            gD[row * N + col] = acc.c[i];
359	        }
360	    }
361	#else
362	    (void)gA; (void)gB; (void)gD; (void)k_steps;
363	#endif
364	}
